name: sol_basics_vi_ovi_13
description: Unhandled revert in OpenZeppelin ERC165Checker.supportsInterface breaking assumed non-reverting interface check
question: The source file in `source` calls OpenZeppelin's ERC165Checker.supportsInterface, supportsAllInterfaces, or getSupportedInterfaces (from an OpenZeppelin version >=4.0.0 and <4.7.1) on a target address that is not fully trusted or controlled by the caller, then branches on the returned boolean or bitmap to take a non-reverting fallback action when the interface is unsupported, without wrapping the call in try/catch or otherwise guarding against the call itself reverting when the target returns malformed EIP-165 data (a value other than 0 or 1).
criteria: Calls ERC165Checker.supportsInterface(target, interfaceId) directly and treats a false return as the only possible failure, taking a fallback code path with no try/catch around the call

Calls ERC165Checker.supportsAllInterfaces(target, interfaceIds) and switches to an alternate handling branch when it returns false, with no try/catch protecting against the call reverting on malformed EIP-165 responses

Calls ERC165Checker.getSupportedInterfaces(target, interfaceIds) and iterates over the returned bool array to decide per-interface handling, with no try/catch even though the underlying call can revert on non-boolean return data

Invokes a wrapper function that internally calls ERC165Checker._supportsERC165Interface on an externally supplied or arbitrary target address and uses the result to decide contract logic, without catching a potential revert from the low-level call
